exploration.title: Solar System Explorer
exploration.subject: Space science
exploration.summary: Tour the eight planets and compare their distances from the Sun and the lengths of their years.
exploration.question: How different are the worlds that share our Sun?
exploration.explanation: The eight planets orbit the Sun, which is a star. Their sizes, distances and orbital periods vary greatly. An astronomical unit, or AU, is about the average Earth–Sun distance. This is a schematic: planet sizes and orbit distances use different scales, paths are simplified circles and positions are illustrative, not today’s sky.

experiments.title: Compare orbital periods
experiments.instruction: Predict which completes more of its orbit in one Earth year: Earth or Neptune. Select your prediction, then Advance one Earth year.
experiments.observe: Earth completes 1 orbit and Neptune about 1/165. Explain why equal elapsed time does not mean equal orbital fractions.

experiments.title: Compare diameters
experiments.instruction: Predict how many Earth diameters fit across Jupiter. Choose Jupiter, then View: True diameter comparison. Keep the same view while comparing other planets.
experiments.observe: Jupiter spans about 11.21 Earth diameters. Explain why the separate close-up cannot establish this ratio.

exploration.misconception: Planets are not evenly spaced, and a convenient orbit diagram cannot show both true planet sizes and true gaps at the same scale.
